title: Parental Love
paragraphs: “W-Wh… What!? What the hell is this!?”
The Filolial rancher was so shocked that they almost fell over, barely managing to steady themselves by leaning against the Filolial they had brought along.
“What is this skeleton structure!? Is this really… a Filolial?”

The rancher staggered toward Yuki-chan, alternating their gaze between Kou and Sakura-chan. Then, with practiced hands, they began examining Yuki-chan’s beak, neck, chest, and feathers, and thoroughly inspected her ankles.

“Her body shape has changed significantly, but she still retains the traits of a Filolial. And the scent… No way… Could it be…? No, no, are you telling me this is the master of the legendary Filolial!?”
“Ah, to reach that conclusion so quickly—just as expected from someone acknowledged by Motoyasu.”
“When it comes to knowledge, they might not be too far behind Melty-chan.”
Despite my displeasure, the rancher was wide-eyed with astonishment.
“Why couldn’t you tell at a glance?”
“I’ve heard of monsters that can take human form, but a Filolial that can do that? That’s the stuff of fairy tales!”
“Well, considering this world is already another world, what does it matter…”
“Compared to us who came from a modern society, yeah.”
“We might not fully understand, but there’s probably some kind of boundary somewhere.”
“I… get the feeling.”
For some reason, Éclair was nodding in agreement with the rancher’s astonishment.
What’s that supposed to mean?
“Ah, for example, there’s this story… about a merchant who raised a Filolial with great care for their business, and it had to be of the opposite gender.”
“What’s that supposed to mean?”
“It’s from a light novel I read a long time ago. Of course, it’s just a fairy tale, but the Filolial would take human form and become the merchant’s bride.”
“I’ve heard that before. But it’s not just Filolials—there are countless variations involving dragons and griffins too.”
“There’s also the story of a Filolial repaying a debt, since they’re birds.”
“That exists.”
Éclair seems to have a surprising amount of knowledge about fairy tales.
Did she hear these stories as a child?
“She seems to have all the interspecies marriage tales covered. Well, this is a fantasy world after all.”
“Since monsters capable of taking human form actually exist, and with demi-humans and beastmen around, it’s not that strange at all.”
For some reason, Ren concluded the conversation. His gaze drifted toward Sakura-chan and the mole.
“Pleased to meet you. I am Yuki, a Filolial who serves under Lord Motoyasu and pulls their carriage. The Filolials with me are Kou and Sakura.”
Yuki-chan introduced herself politely to the rancher.
“A Filolial that can take human form and even speak… Could this be from one of the eggs I sold…?”
In response to the rancher’s question, I nodded.
“Yuki-chan was born from one of the high-priced eggs. The other two are Kou and Sakura-chan.”
“I see…”
The rancher stared intently at Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan.
“The guy who said he’d make them into legendary Filolials and bought them really came back with them… Who the hell are you…?”
“I am the Love Hunter, Motoyasu Kitamura!”

“Uh, since it seems you bought them without introducing yourself, let me explain. We’re the Four Cardinal Heroes, and shortly after being summoned to this world, we came here and bought the Filolials with your help.”
The rancher looked at us with an expression of half amazement, half disbelief.
“Th-Then, the rumor about the Four Cardinal Heroes traveling with the Divine Bird is…”
“Yes. It’s about us. And those Filolials were actually purchased here.”
“Indeed!”
The rancher had an expression that was a mix of being impressed and overwhelmed at my words.
“I was impressed by your enthusiasm for Filolials, but… this is beyond what I imagined…”
They were giving Yuki-chan a very thorough examination.
“She’s the picture of perfect health. I was worried that her combination might lead to some weakness, though.”
“I won’t succumb to any illness!”
Yuki-chan puffed out her chest with pride. How admirable.
“So… this place ended up being a ranch that produced the Divine Bird without even knowing it… Huh…”
The rancher nodded to themselves several times.
“Could it be that when a hero raises them, they undergo some kind of special growth…?”
“Oh! Exactly! When raised by a hero, Filolials can transform into these angelic forms!”
“You’re quick to catch on. This should make things move along more smoothly.”
As Father murmured, he seemed to lock eyes with the rancher.
“Well then. From here on, this is going to be a business conversation, and it’s going to get pretty long. Wouldn’t you like to be part of something big?”
Father gave a fearless grin as he spoke.

What is this? Aren’t we supposed to be comrades who share the great mission of raising Filolials? Even the rancher, not wanting to lose to Father’s intense gaze, returned the grin and extended a hand for a handshake.
“Interesting… I feel like I need to hear all about this in detail.”
“Motoyasu, you know better than anyone that Naofumi is the best person to handle this kind of negotiation, right?”
“Yes, we should leave it to Naofumi-san and just observe.”
“But we’re here to buy out all the Filolials, aren’t we!?”
I don’t think it’s just my imagination that I smell business in the air. But the important thing here is the Filolials, and above all, Filo-tan. Father, I need you to understand that.
“It’s fine. You understand that it’s not just about money, right? I have an acquaintance who’s an alchemist and wants to study Filolials. I was hoping to talk to you as the person in charge… I say.”

“Ah, there’s something more important than money. No, there’s a value here that money can’t buy. If this works out, even sickly Filolials could become healthier, faster, and more unique… It could be the key to ushering in a new era…”
The rancher closed his eyes, as if he were lost in a world of imagination. What a wonderful expression.
But my love for Filolials is second to none! Rather, this is the moment for me to speak!
“Ugh… Motoyasu! Stand down!”
“It’s easier if we leave this to Naofumi-san.”
“Fuhahahaha! I cannot back down from this!”
I can’t just leave this matter entirely in Father’s hands.

Neither Ren nor Itsuki can stop me! And so, the rancher led us to a large house. The room had a stronger research vibe than last time. There were several sheets that looked like pedigrees scattered around the corner of the room.
“So, what business do you have at my ranch?”
“There are several things… but first, what is it that you desire?”
“Well… securing a bloodline of healthy and capable Filolials, I suppose?”

I feel like the rancher glanced sharply at Yuki-chan and the others. Yuki-chan noticed the gaze and hid behind me. Sakura-chan, doing the same, tried to hide behind Father, though not very successfully. As for Kou… he was just looking around curiously.
“Looks like everyone except Kou isn’t too keen on this.”
“Is something happening?”
“Maybe you’ll understand during the matchmaking, Kou.”
“Mating?”
“W-What did you say, Kou-san?”
“Do you even know what that means?”
Itsuki and Ren questioned Kou. Filolials instinctively understand these things.
Ugh… Could it be that Kou is entering his mating season? I need to find him a good bride, don’t I?
“Breeding, right? Yuki and Sakura don’t like it. Can Kou do it with his song and dance?”
“Is this where we start to see how different their understanding is from ours?”
“I don’t know, but I really don’t want to see or hear this. Is this what they call parental instinct?”
“Motoyasu, what do you think about this?”
“Kou, you must find a good wife…”
“He understands…”
“I don’t get Motoyasu’s standards! I thought this was like a parent’s feelings when marrying off their son or daughter!”
Ren was groaning about something. He doesn’t get it. A parent only wishes for their children’s happiness.
